items.stem: What is the key limitation to remember when using AI output in a business or product claim?

options.text: AI output can be plausible but wrong, so claims and figures must be verified
options.rationale: Correct: AI can fabricate; verification is essential.

options.text: AI output is always correct and needs no review
AI removes the need for professional judgement
options.rationale: Judgement and accountability remain with the professional.
AI can process text; the issue is accuracy.

items.stem: Which TWO are sound governance practices for AI in a small-business team? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Classifying data before entering it into AI tools
options.rationale: Correct: data classification prevents confidential information from leaking.

options.text: Keeping an audit trail of AI-assisted outputs
options.rationale: Correct: an audit trail supports review and accountability.

options.text: Entering confidential data into any public tool
Publishing AI output without any review
options.rationale: Unreviewed AI output is a control failure.

items.explanation: Correct: classifying data before use and keeping an audit trail of AI-assisted outputs are sound AI governance practices.

items.stem: To make an AI-drafted product or marketing passage reliable, the best practice is to:

options.text: Ground the draft in supplied source material and verify key details
options.rationale: Correct: grounding plus verification reduces fabrication risk.

options.text: Ask the model to write it from memory
Trust the first output without checking

options.rationale: Length alone does not ensure reliability.
